_note: The documented wire contract between this server and the TOSCA-2 collab frontend. Every shape here is taken from the frontend's own guards in src/collab/stores/collabTracking.ts (isRawMarkerDictionary / isTrackingFeatureCollection / isCalibrationAck, parseRawMarkerSnapshot, buildMapCalibrationFromMarkerReadings) and from known_good_map_calibration_2026-08-31.json, the handshake the operator confirmed working on the live rig. Backend contract tests read this file rather than restating the JSON inline, so the two sides cannot drift apart silently.

map_calibration._note: points are ordered by MAP_CALIBRATION_MARKERS, i.e. 200, 201, 202, 203. lat_lon_position is [lat, lng]. Pixel positions below are the operator-confirmed 2026-08-31 readings.

clear_calibration._note: Drops the homography so the raw marker feed resumes; this is how the frontend re-enters calibration.

building_calibration._note: Per-building residual, sent when the operator saves a nudge in the admin panel. Any subset of the four fields may be present; the server merges them onto what is already stored, so an untouched axis is never reset. Units are the OPERATOR's: table millimetres (1 table pixel = 1 mm at 10 px/cm, one arrow-key tick) and degrees. The offsets are expressed in the BUILDING's own local east/north frame, so they turn with the block rather than with the compass. Python converts millimetres to the catalog's real-world metres via physical_building_catalog.calibration_from_message, which is what keeps MODEL_SCALE = 500 a Python-only number. No table position and no session id are sent: Python owns pixel space and stamps the measurement with the marker's own latest reading. Refused unless a map_calibration is in force, the marker is in the catalog, building_id agrees with the marker, and the marker has actually been seen on the table.

raw_marker_snapshot._note: Plain object keyed by marker id; each value is [pixel_x, pixel_y, rotation, camera_or_tag]. Sent while no basemap homography is configured. JSON object keys are strings; the frontend does Number(key), so numeric ids survive the round trip. An empty object is valid and means 'nothing on the table'.

building_geojson._note: Sent once a basemap homography exists. Only ids present in physical-building-catalog.json become features, so calibration markers 200-203 never appear here. An empty FeatureCollection is still a valid, meaningful message (it proves Python is on the calibrated feed). Each feature's properties carry marker_id, building_id, city_scope_id, center, rotation (detected - marker_reference + rotation_offset_deg), model_scale_factor (the session's global k times the building's scale_residual), bbox, and table_x_px/table_y_px -- where the marker was seen in table-pixel space, which is what lets the admin panel draw its table-coverage diagram. `model_scale` is the blocks' milling scale (500), published so the panel can work in table millimetres without restating it.
